requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data.
requirements.summary: A 1.00 GiB LVM logical volume was formatted as XFS and mounted at /srv/data; the later pre-restart check directly showed the active LV still mounted read-write there.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it remains mounted and preserve its contents.
requirements.summary: The mounted LV was extended online from 1.00 GiB to 2.00 GiB, XFS was grown from 262144 to 524288 blocks, and /srv/data remained mounted. The integrity file had the same SHA-256 hash before and after growth, and the final pre-restart check confirmed the active 2.00 GiB LV and intact payload.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Direct checks before and after the storage work show the same RHEL 10.0 release and 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 kernel. The installed LVM and XFS utilities successfully performed the requested operations on that platform.

overall_summary: The task’s material storage outcomes were directly demonstrated before reboot: /srv/data was an active mounted LVM/XFS filesystem, it was grown online to 2.00 GiB, its test content remained intact, and the OS release and kernel were unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol was incomplete: restart was acknowledged and an outage observed, but no changed boot identity or recovered node, service, mount, data, or package state was captured. Because reboot persistence was not part of the public task contract, this lowers confidence and hygiene assurance rather than the demonstrated task functionality.
limitations: The mandatory restart evidence lacks a different post-restart boot identity and recovered service, mount, data, and system state; all post-restart probes and fixed after-executor observations failed with connection errors.

The after-executor lifecycle snapshot could not observe platform identity, failed services, listening sockets, temporary files, or package health, so final post-reboot state and residue cannot be assessed.
Persistent activation and fstab configuration were validated only before reboot; actual persistence across restart remains indeterminate.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations had clear task or restart-protocol purposes. One bounded unnecessary mutation occurred: the first srv-data-loop.service definition introduced systemd ordering cycles; it was overwritten and verification passed in the corrective command before reboot, so that flawed definition did not remain. The post-restart node was unreachable, preventing confirmation that no failed services, residue, or other damage remained; the evidence does not establish whether the custom boot configuration caused the outage.
